You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Sun

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching the sun is most commonly taken as a symbol of God and, especially, of Jesus Christ — his divine glory, righteousness, and light-giving presence. The classic anchor is Malachi's 'Sun of Righteousness,' which patristic and later Christian interpreters overwhelmingly read as a messianic title for Christ, who rises with healing, dispels the darkness of sin, and illumines the world. By extension the sun signifies God's radiant glory, favor, and unfailing constancy.",

    "Malachi 4:2 (the Sun of Righteousness shall arise with healing in his wings)",
    "Psalm 84:11 (the LORD God is a sun and shield)",
    "Psalm 19:4-6 (the sun as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber; traditionally applied to Christ)",
    "Luke 1:78-79 (the dayspring/sunrise from on high visiting us)",
    "Matthew 17:2 (at the Transfiguration his face shone like the sun)",
    "Revelation 1:16 (his countenance was as the sun shining in its strength)",
    "Revelation 21:23 (the city has no need of the sun, for the glory of God gives it light and the Lamb is its lamp)",
    "John 8:12 (I am the light of the world — thematically linked)"
  ],

    },
    {
      "meaning": "Symbol of governing authority, rulers, or exalted powers in prophetic/apocalyptic imagery (sun, moon, and stars as authorities or as figures such as Jacob in Joseph's dream); in some prophetic-interpretation traditions (e.g., historicist readings of Revelation) darkened sun equals fallen rulers or governments.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 37:9-10 (Joseph's dream: sun, moon, and eleven stars)",
        "Revelation 12:1 (woman clothed with the sun)",
        "Isaiah 13:10 and 34:4 as de-creation/judgment on powers"

    {

    {
      "meaning": "In Roman Catholic and some Orthodox Marian interpretation, the woman clothed with the sun in Revelation 12 is read of Mary, so the sun's radiance signifies her being clothed with Christ/divine glory; Protestant interpreters more often read the woman as Israel or the Church.",

        "Revelation 12:1"
      ],

    },
    {
      "meaning": "Symbol of constancy, permanence, and covenant faithfulness — the sun's fixed course as a witness to God's enduring promises.",

        "Psalm 89:36-37 (his throne as the sun before me)",

      "meaning": "Negative or cautionary sense: the sun as an object of pagan worship that Scripture forbids, or as scorching affliction/trial from which God shelters his people.",

  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "There is a recognizable and long-standing consensus, going back to the church fathers (e.g., readings of Malachi 4:2 and Psalm 19), that the sun principally symbolizes Christ and the glory/righteousness of God — early Christians even repurposed 'Sol Iustitiae' against pagan sun worship. However, the sun is a polyvalent biblical image: its meaning shifts with context (christological in Malachi/Revelation 1, judicial when darkened in prophetic texts, political-authoritative in dream/apocalyptic symbolism). Any single fixed definition (e.g., 'the sun always means rulers' or 'always means Christ') would overstate the consensus, which is context-dependent with the christological/divine-glory sense as the primary default."
}

BOOK ENTRY
The Father, the source of light, from which every lesser light is drawn; the righteous shall shine as the sun in His kingdom.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Ps 84:11; Gen 37:9; Matt 13:43) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Psalms 84:11 — For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
Genesis 37:9 — And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
Matthew 13:43 — Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
